title: Tenant-aware SLO decomposition, dynamic shedding, and multi-region failover playbook
creator: Marcelo Ortega
description: Goal: Produce a concrete, implementable playbook that ties per-endpoint and per-model SLIs to tenant-weighted SLOs, defines automated circuit-breaker triggers based on error-budget velocity, and prescribes multi-region failover and adaptive load-shedding policies. This ticket covers definition, runbook, alerting thresholds, and a set of example mappings (chat, completions, embeddings, reranking). Deliverables: canonical SLI definitions, error-budget burn profiles, circuit-breaker parameter table, regional escalation timeline, tenant-priority degradation matrix, monitoring dashboards links, and a reference GitHub PR to implement enforcement hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI document exists and is approved by Reliability and Product (PRD link included)
Error budget burn-rate rules and circuit-breaker thresholds are codified in a YAML snippet and signed-off by SRE
Multi-region escalation timeline (primary -> warm standby -> full failover) defined with detection windows and automated routing changes
Tenant-aware shedding policy established with example mappings for Platinum/Gold/Silver/pluggable workspaces
Dashboards and alerts created in Grafana with runbook links and test plan for simulated regional degradation
A reference implementation PR created that wires the circuit-breaker hooks to the runtime and policy engine
slis_and_slos_summary: Availability SLI (per endpoint/model): success_rate = 1 - (5xx_count + internal_timeout_count) / total_requests. Baseline SLOs: low-latency routes (chat-lite): 99.95% monthly; heavy-generation routes (long-completions): 99.8% monthly.
Latency SLI (P95/P99): measurement windows are request-level tail latencies excluding queued time. Example SLOs: chat-lite P95 < 250ms, P99 < 550ms; embeddings P95 < 200ms, P99 < 500ms.
Quality SLI (for structured outputs): measured via synthetic evals and promptsets; quality SLOs are separate and tied to canary rollouts (see canary_playbook link).
Combined SLI contract: composition of availability + latency buckets per route with weightings applied by tenant priority (see tenant-weighting matrix below).
error_budget_and_burn_policy: Standard error-budget window: 30d rolling for booking and monthly reporting.

Burn-rate detection windows and automated actions: if burn_rate_6h > 3x => open P1 and trigger adaptive throttling; if burn_rate_6h > 6x => enable failover slice and raise circuit breaker; if burn_rate_1h > 10x => immediate throttling to preserve cluster health.
Error budget allocation: per-endpoint and per-model buckets; tenant affinity slices reserve up to 20% of an endpoint's error budget for Platinum tenants to avoid eviction during temporary surges.
Reclaim rules: unused reserved slices decay after 72 hours of underutilization unless manually extended by SRE.
circuit_breaker_spec: Primary triggers: 5xx rate > 2% sustained for 3 minutes OR P99 latency > 5x SLO for 5 minutes.
Secondary validation: validate that error budget burn rate > 2x before full circuit-breaker escalation to prevent false positives from noisy metrics.

Breaker actions by severity: soft (route-level reject with 503 to lowest-priority tenants), medium (route-level shedding + route-specific fallback to small-model variant), hard (regional ejection of route and re-routing to warm-standby region).
Cooldown and retry: exponential backoff with jitter; initial test probe after 30s, progressive ramp at 10%/30%/60% of prior qps if successful.
Operational hooks: circuit-breaker state published to event bus and visible in Console with origin, threshold that triggered, and list of affected tenants.
multi_region_failover_and_escalation: Detection: cross-region QoS divergence metric computed as normalized SLI delta per 1m window. If primary region's combined SLI drops below regional-slo-threshold for 2 consecutive 1m windows and error_budget burn high, begin warm-standby routing.
Warm-standby: shift 10% traffic to secondary region for 10 minutes and monitor for improvement; if improvement < 30% then escalate to 50% and prepare full failover.

Full failover: automated DNS/routing update with traffic cutover to secondary; maintain sticky routing for continuing sessions where KV cache transfer is possible, otherwise prefer per-request stateless fallbacks.
Data considerations: ensure telemetry tags include original_region and tenant_priority; for sensitive customers on Private/VPC, follow manual approval workflow rather than automated cutover.
tenant_priority_and_shedding_matrix: Priority tiers: Platinum, Gold, Silver, Free.
Shedding rules (example): under medium degradation: Free -> 100% reject; Silver -> 50% reject + sampling responses; Gold -> 10% sampling; Platinum -> no reject unless hard breaker.
Model degradation preference: first degrade to quantized/2-bit or small-variant models for non-Platinum tenants; for Platinum, prefer latency-preserving quantization and reserve cache hits.
Billing signal integration: when shedding occurs log event into billing pipeline for later credits/communications.
monitoring_alerting_and_runbooks: Alerts: SLO burn-rate (1h/6h/24h), P95/P99 latency shifts, 5xx spikes, regional SLI delta, circuit-breaker state changes.
Runbooks: step-by-step mitigation actions for soft, medium, and hard events; resident oncall must follow the runbook and update incident channel with 'slo-playbook' tag.
Testing: include synthetic chaos tests to periodically trigger warm-standby and circuit-breaker probes in staging; add integration tests for tenant-shedding mappings.
Observability: provide per-tenant SLI dashboards and a 'what-if' simulator in Console to model shedding outcomes prior to policy changes.
implementation_notes: Short-term scope: produce canonical doc + Grafana dashboards + skeletal PR that wires policy to the policy engine. Target: ship in 2 sprints.
Medium-term scope: integrate with Console for manual overrides, and wire to billing for automated credits when shedding occurs.
Engineering trade-offs: aggressive eviction preserves cluster health but degrades UX for downstream customers—policy must be conservative in default and tuned per workspace via Console.
Open questions: exact burn-rate multipliers for small endpoints, telemetry cardinality cost of per-tenant SLIs, and opt-in flow for Private customers.
